Question: The area of a rectangle remains unchanged when it is made \(2\dfrac12\) inches longer and \(\dfrac23\) inch narrower, or when it is made \(2\dfrac12\) inches shorter and \(\dfrac43\) inch wider. Its area, in square inches, is:
Solution:
Let the original length and width be \(L\) and \(W\) inches. The shortened and narrowed rectangles must have positive dimensions, so \(L>5/2\) and \(W>2/3\).

Each modified rectangle has the original area \(LW\), giving
\[
\left(L+\frac52\right)\left(W-\frac23\right)=LW,
\]
\[
\left(L-\frac52\right)\left(W+\frac43\right)=LW.
\]
Expanding is useful because the shared term \(LW\) cancels. After cancellation and multiplication by \(6\), the equations become
\[
15W-4L=10,
\qquad
8L-15W=20.
\]
Adding eliminates \(W\), leaving \(4L=30\), so \(L=15/2\). Substituting into the first equation gives \(15W-30=10\), hence \(W=8/3\).

These dimensions satisfy the required positivity conditions. The modified dimensions are \(10\) by \(2\), and \(5\) by \(4\), so both modified areas are indeed \(20\). The original area is
\[
LW=\frac{15}{2}\cdot\frac83=20
\]
square inches, choice \(\mathrm{E}\).
